subject: Dynamic thurstonian model using mirt - is it possible?

messages.author: 498625331dc5ad8c
messages.subject: Dynamic thurstonian model using mirt - is it possible?
parts:
Dear all, 
we are estimating dynamic thurstonian model using mirt. We have successfully estimated the non-dynamic model, but I am afraid the dynamic model is not possible within mirt (and I want to be sure). We have three possible nominal answers (say, A, B, and C) across 15 items and we suppose there are three latent traits. Using gpcm_mats, I defined which trait saturated which response type. That was quite easy. 

Unfortunately, the problem is the dynamic part. Assume that an answer A on item 1 reduces the probability to answer A again on item 2. Thus, I want to include some person:item covariates to store the information about previous observed responses.  

Using mixedmirt function, I can include both item covariates (aka explanatory LLTM model) and person covariates (aka latent regression). However, I need to include some interaction between person and item. 

I can estimate the model using lme4 package, but mirt provides me the possibility to estimate 2PL model and get fit indices (M2 statistics). Is there any way to do it in mirt?
Hynek

messages.subject: Re: Dynamic thurstonian model using mirt - is it possible?
parts:
Dear Phil, 

I apologize for the delay; my spam filter decided I shouldn't receive your response, and I wasn't checking here online. We are doing a re-analysis of the OMT test, the original paper here: 

Runge, J. M., Lang, J. W., Engeser, S., Schüler, J., den Hartog, S. C., & Zettler, I. (2016). Modeling motive activation in the Operant Motive Test: A psychometric analysis using dynamic Thurstonian item response theory. Motivation Science, 2(4), 268. https://doi.org/10.1037/mot0000041

The lme4 model is described there (models M3 and M4), but their description is too complicated. 

However, I solved the problem in the meantime using two different approaches.

  1. Using a bifactor structure with specific factors, which model residual dependency between items.
  2. Defining my item response function using createSyntax function, which is fantastic! I provided additional covdata, which does the job.  

Unfortunately, we probably won't use these more advanced models in our paper, and I stopped elaborating on them a few months ago. The data are messy anyway; and while even the simplest model fits them very well, the reliability is negligible.
